signIn.intro: A personalized health and fitness tracker that connects with your Google Health data. It establishes rolling baselines and presents actionable trend analysis to help you understand your body better.
signIn.expired: Your Google connection has expired or was revoked. Reconnect to resume syncing; your stored data is still here.
signIn.notInvited: This Healthier instance is invite-only, and that Google account is not on its list. Ask whoever runs it to add you.
signIn.failed: Google sign-in failed ({code}). Check the server logs for details.
signIn.disclosure: Healthier reads your health and fitness data from Google Health (activity, sleep, heart rate, vitals and body measurements) to show your trends, work out your personal baselines and generate insights. It is stored only on the server running this app, used for nothing else, and never shared. You can disconnect and delete it at any time from the Data tab.
signIn.wellness: For general wellness only. Healthier is not a medical device and doesn't diagnose, detect or monitor any condition.

how.explainer: Compares each night's average oxygen, breathing rate and time awake with your own usual range. A night counts when two of them are off together, and a pattern needs several such nights in the last two weeks — never one bad night.
how.footer: Uses nightly average oxygen saturation, breathing rate and time awake as your device reports them. Wrist sensors miss a lot during sleep, so a quiet card doesn't rule anything out.

how.explainer: One metric can move because of a late meal or a warm room. When several move at once, it's a clearer sign that something changed: often recovery, sometimes a cold coming on.

how.footer: Counts how many of resting heart rate, breathing rate, skin temperature and HRV are outside your usual range on the latest day. Several at once often follows hard training, short sleep, alcohol, heat or travel, or feeling under the weather.

dip.watch: Watches how far your heart rate falls from daytime to non-REM sleep over 30 days.
dip.light: Lights up when half or more of the measured nights drop less than 10%.

how.explainer: Heart rate usually drops during sleep compared with the daytime, often by 10–20%. This tracks your own drop over the last 30 days. Late meals, alcohol, heat, evening exercise and illness all shift it from night to night, so only a multi-week change is shown.
how.footer: Daytime is the 08:00–20:00 average of your minute-level heart rate; night is your non-REM sleeping heart rate. A 10% drop is a night/day ratio of 0.90. The 10% and 20% lines come from overnight blood-pressure research and are only a rough guide for heart rate.

tachy.watch: Watches minute-level heart rate through recorded sleep and naps, skipping minutes awake.

how.explainer: Lists stretches of recorded sleep where your heart rate stayed above 100 bpm for ten minutes or more. Fever, alcohol, vivid dreams, waking and movement can all do this.
how.footer: Uses the one-minute heart-rate averages synced from your watch. Wrist readings during sleep can be noisy, and movement or waking raises them.

hint.day: Each block is a day: solid where the stream has an observation. Gaps are days the API returned nothing (or the sentinel 'zero' that means missing).
hint.week: Each block is a week, shaded by how many of its days have an observation: solid is all seven.
hint.month: Each block is a month, shaded by how many of its days have an observation.

intraday.hintWeekly: Minutes of heart rate recorded in each hour, averaged per week over the {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} minute data is kept. Gaps show when the watch is usually off.

arithmetic.text: Your body battery, sleep score and insights are worked out with plain arithmetic from your own data. Nothing is written or guessed by AI. Sleep stages and cardio fitness are your watch's own estimates.

usual.text: Anything called usual or unusual is compared with your own last {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}, not with other people. One odd day won't change what's normal for you.

window.text: {history, select, shown {Your insights and most charts use your window, the last {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}. {viewCount, plural, one {The {views} view adds your history, back to {month}.} other {The {views} views add your history, back to {month}.}} Every sync re-checks the last {refetch, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}, because watches often send data late.} other {Your insights and most charts use your window, the last {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}. Every sync re-checks the last {refetch, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}, because watches often send data late.}}

missing.text: A day with nothing recorded shows a dash, not a zero, and is left out of every average. Today so far joins your averages once the day is over.

minutes.text: Your watch measures your heart rate every few seconds. Healthier keeps one average per minute for the heart rate charts and Labs, so very short spikes are smoothed out.

streams.title: Data streams
streams.hint: Everything Healthier reads from Google Health, and whether it's arriving. Open one to see where it comes from and what happened on the last fetch.

detail.occasional: {source, select, hand {Last reading {when}, logged by hand.} device {Last reading {when}, from {device}.} other {Last reading {when}.}} These come now and then, so a gap since the last one is normal.
detail.latestReading: {source, select, hand {Latest reading {when}, logged by hand.} device {Latest reading {when}, from {device}.} other {Latest reading {when}.}} {coverage}
detail.latestMinute: {source, select, hand {Latest minute {when}, logged by hand.} device {Latest minute {when}, from {device}.} other {Latest minute {when}.}} {coverage}
detail.behind: Nothing new since {date}. Healthier asks for it on every sync, so it fills in as soon as your device records it again.
detail.empty: Google has no readings of this for you: none of your devices record it, or nothing has been logged.
detail.unshared: Healthier wasn't given access to this when you connected Google, so it doesn't ask for it. To add it, sign out, sign back in and allow it when Google asks.
detail.unauthorized: Google refused access to this on the last fetch. If you didn't allow it when connecting, sign out, sign back in and allow it.
detail.failed: Google answered the last fetch with an error, so the days already stored stay as they were. Healthier tries again on the next sync.
detail.truncated: {detail} Google had more readings than one fetch takes, so some older ones may be missing.
